item.title: CedarLogic 0.3 (build 751)
item.description:
CedarLogic 0.3 for Mac

A new name (just CedarLogic), a new icon, and a lot more inside. After you update, a short What's New tour walks you through all of it (Help ▸ What's New in CedarLogic brings it back).

Your circuits, in one place

  • Every circuit lives in Your Circuits (⌘O) and saves itself as you go. Open, rename and delete from there, or rename the one you're in from its name at the top.
  • Opening a .cdl file brings in a copy to work on; File ▸ Export as CedarLogic File… gets one out.
  • Version history only keeps a version when the circuit itself changed, not every time a switch flips.

Start ahead

  • File ▸ New from Template…: a Lab Page with your name on it, a 4-bit counter, a 7-segment decoder starter, or your own (Save as Template…). Settings ▸ General can start every new circuit from one.
  • My Parts: select some gates, Edit ▸ Save as Part…, name it. Drag it from the side panel or find it with A.

Check your work

  • The truth table (T) has tabs: the table, a Karnaugh map for each light, and the simplest sum of products and product of sums.
  • Edit ▸ Build from Formula… turns F = AB + C' (or Σm(…)) into wired, labelled gates.
  • Find (⌘F) searches labels, TO/FROM names and parts on every page.

See it think

  • Point at a wire and every branch of it lights up (Settings ▸ Canvas can show what it carries).
  • Share the oscilloscope (⌘G) as a timing diagram: copy, PNG or PDF, in colour or black and white.

A new look

  • CedarLogic green, the icon's colour, is the app's colour now (Settings ▸ Appearance ▸ App colour has the others).
  • A new welcome and guided tour, and cleaner editors for gate settings and memory (double-click a gate or a RAM; Return is Done).
  • ⌘Q asks first (Settings ▸ General ▸ Quitting), and Send Feedback (the speech bubble) takes a note, a screenshot or a short recording.

Fixes

  • The first ⌘A, ⌘N or ⌘Q after launch works; the Edit menu no longer flickers.
  • Dropping certain pasted circuits no longer crashes.
  • Your Circuits' Delete and Rename work every time, and the highlight stays on the circuit you chose.
  • Circuit windows open on the screen you launched from.

item.title: CedarLogic 0.2.6 (build 750) beta
item.description:
• Truth tables (T) have tabs: the table, a Karnaugh map for every light with its groups drawn on, and each light's simplest sum of products and product of sums. A new look to match the app.
  • Edit > Build from Formula: type F = A'B + AC (or Σm(1,3,5)) and get the switches, gates and lights, wired and labelled. Any gates, NAND only or NOR only.
  • The oscilloscope (Cmd-G) copies or saves a timing diagram for lab reports, in colour or black and white.
  • Pointing at a wire lights up all of it. Settings > Canvas can also show what it carries (0, 1, floating, conflict).
  • Find (Cmd-F): labels, TO/FROM names and parts on every page.
  • Cmd-Q asks first (Settings > General > Quitting).

item.title: CedarLogic 0.2.5 (build 748) beta
item.description:
• The "Simple" interface is gone; everyone gets the CedarLogic window.
  • Settings > General has an "Opening files" button to make this app the one that opens .cdl files; .cdl files get their own icon.
  • Tidier menus: no Mac window tabs, no Dictation or Emoji items in Edit, and File > Duplicate is now "Duplicate Circuit".

item.title: CedarLogic 0.2.4 (build 747) beta
item.description: • New: Send Feedback — the speech bubble at the right of the toolbar (or Help ▸ Send Feedback…). Write what happened, pick tags and how much it matters, and add a screenshot or a short recording of CedarLogic right from the form. It goes straight to Levi.

item.title: CedarLogic 0.2.3 (build 745) beta
item.description:
CedarLogic Native 0.2.3

  • Fixed: the green window button could start out of place until you clicked the window.

item.title: CedarLogic 0.2.2 (build 744) beta
item.description:
CedarLogic Native 0.2.2

  • Crash reports: the app asks once whether to send a report if it crashes (where it went wrong, never your circuits or name). You can change this in Settings > General.
  • The toolbar's ••• menu (Minimal toolbar) shows its tooltip.
  • The red, yellow and green window buttons are put back in place after moving the window between displays or using full screen.

item.title: CedarLogic 0.2.1 (build 740) beta
item.description:
CedarLogic Native 0.2.1

  • The toolbar works every time. Buttons take every click (even quick or slightly sloppy ones), light up wherever you point at them and show their tooltips. A click no longer nudges the window.
  • The toolbar's empty space behaves like a title bar: drag it to move the window, double-click it to fill the screen, drag a filled window to bring it back to its size. In focus mode the tab strip does the same.
  • Better on battery: while a circuit with a clock runs, the app stops drawing whenever you can't see the window.
  • Export for older CedarLogic: File > Export as V2 (legacy XML)… and Export as V1.x Compatible…, for computers that still have an old version.
  • Split view keys from the classic app: Switch Pane (⌘⌥→) and Close Split (⌘⌥W).
  • Help > Set Up CedarLogic… walks through the settings again.

item.title: CedarLogic 0.2 (build 737) beta
item.description:
CedarLogic Native 0.2

The native Mac app now has the full CedarLogic interface, rebuilt natively (Settings > General > Interface switches back to Simple).

  • A new launch screen, and your last circuit reopens when you start the app.
  • Tabs and split view: drag tabs to reorder (the gap opens where they'll land), down to split the view, or across to the other side. Ctrl+Tab switches tabs.
  • Faster building: drag gates out of the palette, press C while a gate is moving to connect it (Escape takes it back), and see the pin a wire will join.
  • Your work saves itself, with versions kept now and then like Google Docs (File > Version History).
  • Your Circuits (⌘O) and Settings (⌘,) look and work like classic CedarLogic. Every shortcut can be changed.
  • Help (F1): new pages for this app, plus the original CedarLogic Help.
  • Toolbar buttons no longer miss clicks, and the window drags, fills and zooms like any Mac app.
  • Low wires are silver on the dark canvas, easier to tell from the grid.
